sentences.text: Loricatosaurus is a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur, a name meaning "armored lizard".
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial skeleton including vertebrae, limb bones, and armor plates.
Unlike previous reports, no shoulder spine is present in the known material, and any spine-like structure is likely from the tail.
A piece of armor previously described as a parascapular spine is actually a fragmentary tail spine.
The genus is known from only two partial skeletons.
The type species was first discovered in November 1901 by Alfred Leeds at the Fletton brick pit in England.
The remains were originally named Stegosaurus priscus by Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1911.
In 2008, Susannah Maidment and colleagues reclassified the species into a new genus named Loricatosaurus.
The initial discovery included a semi-articulated skeleton with vertebrae, partial limbs, pelvis, and fragmentary dermal armor.
A second specimen was briefly referred to Lexovisaurus in 1957 before being properly described in 1985.
A second specimen from Normandy, France, includes many vertebrae and a dorsal spine.
Loricatosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
Loricatosaurus is classified in the family Stegosauridae.
Loricatosaurus belongs to the parent group Stegosaurinae.
A 2025 analysis recovered Loricatosaurus as the sister taxon to an unnamed Chinese stegosaur within the Stegosaurinae.
Loricatosaurus lived during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in England and France.
Loricatosaurus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
